nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 – Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily, titrate up to 10 mg as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually and after each titration step
medications.purpose: Control hypertension and reduce proteinuria in CKD stage 4
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 recommends an ACE inhibitor or ARB for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension (first_line)

medications.purpose: Slow CKD progression and reduce proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 recommends a SGLT2 inhibitor for CKD with eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m² (first_line)

medications.duration: Lifelong – lipid profile in 12 weeks then annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD (risk‑equivalent condition)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 recommends a statin for all CKD patients (first_line)

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention in eGFR 25 mL/min/1.73 m²
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol or topical analgesia as needed

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of lactic acidosis
Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury in advanced CKD
contraindications.alternative: Choose either an ACE‑I (ramipril) **or** an ARB (losartan), not both
Lamotrigine for mood stabilization if needed

contraindications.reason: High risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy when eGFR <30
contraindications.alternative: Use low‑osmolar contrast with adequate hydration and prophylaxis if imaging is essential

assumptions_warnings: Current blood pressure reading not available – need measurement before and during ACE‑I titration.
Baseline serum potassium and creatinine required before starting ramipril; repeat at 1‑2 weeks and 4 weeks.
Liver function tests (ALT/AST, bilirubin) needed before initiating atorvastatin.
Hemoglobin, ferritin and transferrin saturation not provided – required to decide on ESA therapy for anemia.
Albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio (ACR) not supplied – needed to confirm proteinuria severity and BP target.
Allergy status unknown – must confirm no ACE‑I, statin or SGLT2‑i hypersensitivity.
Pregnancy status not documented – ACE‑I and statin are contraindicated in pregnancy; verify patient is not pregnant.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 2.5 mg daily (titrate to 10 mg) and dapagliflozin 10 mg daily to control hypertension, reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression, plus atorvastatin 20 mg daily for cardiovascular risk reduction. Avoid chronic NSAIDs, metformin, ACE‑I/ARB combination, lithium and unprotected IV contrast. Monitor BP, eGFR, potassium, liver enzymes, lipid profile and anemia parameters; adjust therapy as needed and review annually.
